question: A manager asks whether the new Claude-assisted process means the team can cut its review budget. Which two responses are honest and useful? Select two.
options: A) Share what the pilot actually changed in the cycle time, and what it did not change at all.
B) Confirm that the review budget can be cut right now, since the pilot produced no visible errors.
C) Say that the process is fully reliable, so the manager's confidence in it is not undermined.
D) Explain that review is still needed, because outputs continue to need checking before release.
E) Avoid the question, since discussing limitations now would weaken support for the rollout.
correct_answers: A) Share what the pilot actually changed in the cycle time, and what it did not change at all.
D) Explain that review is still needed, because outputs continue to need checking before release.
explanations: Correct. Reporting both what improved and what did not is what sets an expectation the rollout can actually meet.
Incorrect. Absence of visible errors in a short pilot is weak evidence, and cutting review on it removes the safeguard.
Incorrect. Claiming full reliability is an overstatement, and confidence built on it collapses at the first real error.
Correct. Review remains part of the design, and saying so plainly is the honest answer to a budget question.
Incorrect. Withholding limitations to protect support is exactly the communication failure this competency warns against.
